title: Freezing and Cell Banking Protocol
author: Andrea Argouarch
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8gmhtu6
materials: Tap the pellet to resuspend for freezing

steps.title: Clean hood and turn off UV
steps.instruction: Turn off the UV lights in the biosafety cabinet and wipe all surfaces with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Prepare and label cryovials
steps.instruction: Create cryovial labels in Microsoft Word using Cryo‑Tags (USA Scientific Catalog #9187‑1100), print enough for ~15 vials (ID, date, passage, ~0.5 ×10⁶ cells), arrange vials in a 96‑well 1.5 mL tube holder, spray label sheets with 70 % ethanol, dry, apply to each vial, label the top with ID, and unscrew each cap for easy removal.

steps.title: Gather reagents and consumables
steps.instruction: Clean the following items with 70 % ethanol and bring them into the hood: DPBS (no Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺, Thermo Fisher #14190250), sterile DMEM high‑glucose with pyruvate (Thermo Fisher #11995073) plus Pen‑Strep (Thermo Fisher #15140122) and FBS (VWR #97068‑091), 0.05 % Trypsin‑EDTA (Thermo Fisher #25300062), freezing media (10 % DMSO made from Bio‑Max DMSO #40470005‑2 mixed with 90 % DMEM), disposable hemocytometers (Thermo Fisher #22600100), Trypan Blue 0.4 % (Thermo Fisher #15250061), a T25 flask for karyotyping, a 15 mL conical tube (10 mL media) for KT cells, and a 15 mL conical tube for gDNA collection.

steps.title: Document cell morphology
steps.instruction: At 100 % confluency, acquire 3–4 bright‑field images of the cells, save each as a TIFF file named with the cell line ID and passage number.

steps.title: Rinse cells with DPBS
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL of DPBS to each flask, gently swirl to rinse, and discard the rinse.

steps.title: Detach cells with trypsin
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL of 0.05 % Trypsin‑EDTA to each flask, place the flask in a 37 °C incubator for 3 minutes, tapping the side if needed, until cells detach.

steps.title: Inactivate trypsin
steps.instruction: Add 9 mL of fibroblast growth media to each flask to neutralize the trypsin.

steps.title: Collect cell suspension
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire cell suspension into a 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Rinse flask for gDNA
steps.instruction: Add 12 mL of PBS to the original flask, swirl to collect remaining cells, and transfer this rinse into a 15 mL conical tube designated for gDNA extraction.

steps.title: Measure suspension volume
steps.instruction: Determine the total volume of the cell suspension using a serological pipette and mix gently.

steps.title: Perform trypan blue viability assay
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µL of the cell suspension with 10 µL of 0.4 % Trypan Blue, tap to mix, then load the mixture onto a disposable hemocytometer.

steps.title: Count viable cells
steps.instruction: Count the non‑blue (viable) cells in the four corner grids of the hemocytometer, then calculate total viable cells using the formula: (cell count ÷ 4) × 5 (dilution factor) × 10 000 × ≈25 mL (suspension volume).

steps.title: Determine number of cryovials
steps.instruction: From the total viable cell count, compute the volume needed to obtain 0.5 ×10⁶ cells per mL; this volume equals the number of cryovials required.

steps.title: Spin cell pellets
steps.instruction: Centrifuge both the 50 mL cell‑suspension tube and the 15 mL gDNA tube at 1 000 rpm for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Aspirate supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate the supernatant from both pellets without disturbing the cell or gDNA pellets.

steps.title: Store gDNA pellet
steps.instruction: Place the gDNA pellet at –80 °C until a mycoplasma assay is performed.

steps.title: Add freezing media to cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in freezing media added dropwise, then aliquot 1 mL of this suspension into each pre‑labeled cryovial; spin the KT‑cell pellet (if present) during this step.

steps.title: Freeze cells in Mr. Frosty
steps.instruction: Seal each cryovial tightly, place them in a Mr. Frosty freezing container (Thermo Fisher #5100‑0001), and store the container at –80 °C for 24–48 hours.

steps.title: Transfer to liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: After the –80 °C hold, move all cryovials to liquid nitrogen storage (≈ –190 °C).

steps.title: Freeze backup cells from 6‑well plate
steps.instruction: Harvest cells from a 6‑well plate, add freezing media, place the suspension in a Mr. Frosty for 24–48 hours at –80 °C, then transfer to liquid nitrogen (–190 °C).

steps.title: Clean hood and reactivate UV
steps.instruction: Wipe the biosafety cabinet with 70 % ethanol and turn the UV light back on.

steps.title: Prepare KT cells in T25 flask
steps.instruction: Take 60–100 µL of the DMSO‑containing cell suspension, dilute into 10 mL of fresh media, centrifuge at 1 000 rpm for 5 minutes, aspirate the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of media, and add the suspension to a T25 flask. Incubate the flask at 5 % CO₂, 37 °C. When the culture reaches 40–50 % confluency (≈ 5–6 days), ship the flask to Cell Line Genetics for karyotyping.

steps.title: Turn off UV and clean hood again
steps.instruction: Turn off the UV lights and wipe the hood with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Prepare new T150 flasks
steps.instruction: Clean DPBS, media, and trypsin with 70 % ethanol and bring them into the hood; label two T150 flasks with ID, date, and passage number, then add 28 mL of complete DMEM to each flask.
